claim: The Jews who left Arab countries were not refugees: they left by choice, drawn by Zionism. Only the Palestinians were refugees.

heard.who: Shlomo Hillel, Israeli who led the Iraqi Zionist underground's escape operation, quoted by Yehouda Shenhav (1998)
heard.quote: I do not regard the exodus of Jews from Arab countries as refugees. I do not accept that. The Jews in the Arab countries came because they wanted to come

heard.who: Yated Ne'eman, an anti-Zionist ultra-Orthodox Israeli newspaper, quoted by Yehouda Shenhav
heard.quote: this talk about 'Jewish refugees who were expelled from Arab countries' as opposed to 'Arab refugees who were expelled from the land of Israel' was grating to our journalistic ears

answer: Some Jews who left Arab countries went out of Zionist conviction, and Shlomo Hillel, who led the Iraqi Zionist underground's escape operation, does not call it a refugee flight. But the Palestinians were not the only people displaced in these years. About 800,000 Jews are estimated to have lived in Arab countries around 1948 (DellaPergola counts 945,000 for the Middle East and North Africa), and most left between 1948 and the early 1970s. Reasons differed: Egypt after 1956 saw expulsions, and Iraq let Jews leave only if they gave up their citizenship. Iraq's Jews had also suffered the Farhud pogrom in 1941. In early 1957 the UN High Commissioner for Refugees said refugees from Egypt without their government's protection fell under his mandate; the press reported it as covering Jews. Scholars differ on the word refugee. These are estimates; whether the two cases cancel out these facts do not settle.

could_not_verify: An independent demographic total for departures (as opposed to population stock): DellaPergola's population figure is cited, but he is an Israeli demographer, so every figure here still comes from Israeli or Jewish scholarship or encyclopedias; I found no Arab, UN or non-Israeli demographic count I could read. A 1951 report submitted to the UN (H. Dewey Anderson, via the Center for Israel Education) gives counts but is an advocacy tract by a private author, not a UN count; I did not use it. A person should read the national censuses of Iraq (1947) and Egypt (1947) and Morocco, and any UN demographic study.
Moshe Sicron's arrivals-by-country table counts arrivals in Israel only, so it is not cited for departures.
Country-by-country breakdowns beyond Iraq, Morocco and Egypt from a source other than Encyclopedia.com.

The UN refugee office's 1957 statement (now a record fact): read in the High Commissioner's report A/3585/Rev.1 (the High Commissioner's statement at the 27th meeting, 29 January 1957, and Israel's delegate's reply) and in the Economic and Social Council record of 24 July 1957; the Jewish Telegraphic Agency reported it as a ruling on Jews. The High Commissioner's own words do not name Jews; the UN record names them only in the Israeli and ECOSOC delegates' words. I did not find the UNREF fourth-session report as a separate document (UNHCR pages were blocked); a person should read the 27th meeting's summary record (UN Digital Library) and the UNHCR archive.

Whether anyone readable says in so many words that only Palestinians were refugees: I found no such quote. The claim is therefore stated as what is said: that these Jews were not refugees but came by choice or Zionist conviction (Hillel; Yated Ne'eman).

Facts that do not meet the gate's source rule: none by count (the 1957 record fact has the record plus two readers, one of them the Jewish Telegraphic Agency), but every number on the card is Israeli or Jewish in origin, as above.

FINAL REVIEW (2026-11-20): the Iraq 1950-51 dispute (who was behind the Baghdad incidents and whether they drove the exodus) is not on the card; claimants of 'drawn by Zionism' rely on it, so a person should add a scholarly source for each side. Fact 6: the Stanford page gives 175 killed, not the two counts in the fact; now stated. The 1957 UN statement is dated only by the session (29 January to 4 February 1957); the page does not give the meeting date.
not_claimed: This card does not say Jewish displacement cancels out Palestinian displacement, or that one makes the other acceptable.
It does not claim every Jew who left an Arab country was expelled.
It does not claim the Arab states acted on one plan; it records different cases.
It does not give a settled number; all figures here are estimates.

answer_claims.says: Some Jews who left Arab countries went out of Zionist conviction, and Shlomo Hillel, who led the Iraqi Zionist underground's escape operation, does not call it a refugee flight.
But the Palestinians were not the only people displaced in these years.
About 800,000 Jews are estimated to have lived in Arab countries around 1948 (DellaPergola counts 945,000 for the Middle East and North Africa), and most left between 1948 and the early 1970s.
Reasons differed: Egypt after 1956 saw expulsions, and Iraq let Jews leave only if they gave up their citizenship.
Iraq's Jews had also suffered the Farhud pogrom in 1941.
In early 1957 the UN High Commissioner for Refugees said refugees from Egypt without their government's protection fell under his mandate; the press reported it as covering Jews.
Scholars differ on the word refugee.
These are estimates; whether the two cases cancel out these facts do not settle.

skeptic.notes: Final review after the record rule. Read the UNREF report (A/3585/Rev.1): the High Commissioner's statement at the 27th meeting is quoted exactly; it names no religion, so the Jewish reading rests on the ECOSOC record (the Chinese delegate: 'the High Commissioner had assumed responsibility for Jewish refugees expelled from Egypt', a neutral reader) and the JTA report ('has ruled that Jews exiled from Egypt are refugees'). The record flag on fact 7 is honest: worded as what the record says, with two real readers. Fixed by me: (should-fix, done) the fact gave 29 January as the date of the statement; the page gives only the session, 29 January to 4 February. (should-fix, done) fact 6's third source (Stanford) quoted a sentence about Muslims protecting neighbours, which does not support the death counts; it says 175 killed, now stated with that quote. (should-fix, done) fact 3 put DellaPergola's sentence as being about all immigrants; the page says it applies to 'those who left Arab countries and immigrated to Israel', now worded so. The Iraq population figures differ (135,000 DellaPergola; 160,000 Gale): added to contested from sources already on the card. Heard quotes (Hillel, Yated Ne'eman) are real and strong; no one on the card says 'only the Palestinians were refugees', so the claim as phrased is partly a framing (should-fix for the claim text). Still open: (must-fix) the card omits the Iraq 1950-51 dispute, the strongest evidence for 'drawn by Zionism', and the counter to it; (should-fix) every figure is Israeli or Jewish in origin; no UN, Arab or non-Israeli count; Egypt's expulsions rest on one news source plus ECOSOC. Strongest attack, pro-Palestinian: one-sided provenance of numbers. Pro-Israel: thin evidence of expulsion outside Egypt and Iraq. Status stays draft.
